title: codetospec checkers file
description: What the checks the extractor gives no meaning mean, by check name, as a person pins them from each checker's code (policy.ParseCheckers). JSON, or the same document in YAML. Each entry states one of means, any, all, not, cases or unpinnable; the rules beyond the shape (where subject_arg may stand) are checked by codetospec.

fields.description: What a checker, or one of its parts, states.

means.description: A leaf: what the check means.

content_kind.description: A content scope's content kind: the value the grant must name.

content_kind_arg.description: Which call argument (from 0, the context included), a string literal, names a content scope's content kind.

capability_arg.description: Which call argument (from 0, the context included) names the capability.

subject_arg.description: Which call argument names the user a self, coach, user-scope or relation check is about; on a compound checker, passed to its parts.

relation.description: A relation the caller holds to the resource (or to subject_arg's user): a registry or glossary entry.

attribute.description: A boolean attribute's name: a glossary entry.

part.description: A part of a compound checker.

entry.description: One check's pinned meaning, or why it has none.

item.description: The check filters items of this kind: its meaning says when one is visible.

unpinnable.description: Why the check can't be pinned (cross_service, data_predicate…): its guards are skipped with this reason.

note.description: More on the entry, for people.

call.description: On an item entry: the filter's call-level meaning, when a guard tests the filter itself for one call (its failure, an empty result) rather than one item. A self or coach check here names its subject_arg.

cases.description: A checker whose meaning depends on its call's arguments: the first case whose when_arg the call's arguments match is its meaning; a call matching none has none.

when_arg.description: Argument indexes (from 0, the context included) to the argument's text as written: {"2": "\"admin\""}; "@caller" matches an argument the extractor bound to the request user's kaid, whatever its text.

approx.description: The pin is stricter than the code: it leaves out an allowing path the policy model can't state, so the export denies some requests the code allows, never the reverse.

digest.description: The digest of the checker's definition the entry was written for (policies --src prints it): a different current digest makes the pin stale.

bugs.description: Defects the entry's author found in the checker's code while pinning it: questions for review beside the rules, whatever the pin.

kind.description: The doc comment says what the code doesn't do, or a branch can never run.

detail.description: What and where, in the author's words.
